 Fireball over Chattanooga was a piece of an asteroid, NASA says
 This 2014 image provided by NASA shows a Taurid fireball recorded at the NASA All Sky Fireball Network station in Tullahoma, Tenn. (NASA via AP) 
 By Brooks Mendenhall / Astronomy magazine 
 November 8, 2026 
 4 min read 
 See more of our coverage in your search results.
 Add Times Free Press on Google 
 Residents across East Tennessee reported seeing a brilliant streak of light race across the evening sky Thursday. 
 On Friday, NASA confirmed that the fireball was a small fragment of an asteroid burning up in Earth’s atmosphere, and that it broke apart almost directly over the Chattanooga area.
 The fireball appeared at 7:45 p.m. and was recorded by four NASA all-sky cameras in the region, according to the agency. NASA’s analysis shows the object was roughly 2 inches across and weighed about 6 ounces. 
 It was first spotted 53 miles above Robbinsville, North Carolina, traveling a little south of west at about 47,000 mph. Less than 10 seconds later, it disintegrated 25 miles above East Ridge.
 The timing led some to wonder whether the fireball belonged to the Taurid meteor shower, which is active through much of November and known for bright meteors. NASA says it did not.
